items.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And then I booked Elvin; I booked Rahsaan Roland Kirk, and became a sensation here.

ctx.x: Well, it first started as off-night stuff. And before I started booking five nights a week on Russ Street, I had a place called the North Park Hotel, which is up near Grant Park. I was doing Sunday afternoons and evenings, and they were well attended, and it was all ages. It sat a couple hundred, maybe five hundred in the ballroom. I contacted Yusef, cause I had known him from Chicago, and he said, “well I can’t really” - he was

in Detroit then - “I can’t really come down for one night.” I said, “well...” so we tried Friday, Saturday and Sunday, and it worked. And then I booked Elvin; I booked Rahsaan Roland Kirk, and became a sensation here. Then we had a chance to move. Let’s see, we had a place on Wells Street called the Brown Shoe, which was a huge place. It used to be a restaurant called Paul Bunyan. We then moved to the basement of the Happy Medium at Rush and Delaware, and of course Russ Street was a big entertainment center then.…
